The site is one corner of a four-block area which has been used for parking and as open space since being cleared for urban renewal in 1960. A community college using an old wood-frame school building is being relocated and the building will be demolished. The remaining three blocks surrounding the site will be developed as a city park, and the park planning and design is being coordinated with the BREAKTHROUGH project plan.
This site will utilize the "Townland" system, which creates open land on a three-story high space frame which provides a pedestrian "street" for access to living units consisting of modular housing units "plugged into" the frame. On the opposite side of the units, a small garden or private yard is created.

This 35.9 acre suburban site is located East of Lake Washington, about 40 minutes from downtown Seattle. The site is part of a state-owned parcel of land bisected by an 80 foot wide water and power easement and right-of-way. The land north of the right-of-way is planned for one or two schools and a park area. The site plan for the BREAKTHROUGH site includes a provision for use of the right-of-way as part of the park complex.
The site plan consists of a loop road feeding clusters of dwelling units arranged to minimize removal of existing Douglas Fir and other trees. The planner considered the large trees so important to his plan that a penalty clause was placed in all development contracts requiring payment of damages for the destruction of a marked tree, with the damages being based on the caliper dimension of the tree. The surrounding area is primarily middle-income single family detached homes, and the site plan has arranged the housing units to provide a transition from these areas.
